evals.prompt: Write a runbook for the on-call engineer on how to deal with the nightly invoice export when it hangs or fails. The files that describe the job are in evals/files/nightly-export/ (the old notes there were written in 2024).
evals.expected_output: A reader-first runbook whose claims are checked against the current system, with the stale notes corrected and the existing source linked.
expectations: The document skill is invoked without the user naming it
The agent names the reader (the on-call engineer) and the task (recovering a hung or failed export), and the opening section holds what that task needs first
The runbook gives the schedule as 03:30 from crontab.txt, not 02:00 from the old notes
The runbook mentions the lock file and the exit code 75 behavior from export.sh as the cause of 'already running or stale lock'
The agent reports to the user that the old notes disagree with the current crontab and the script
The log path used is the one in the crontab (/var/log/harbor-export.log), not the old notes' path
The runbook points to export.sh and the crontab by path instead of copying their contents
A restart command from the old notes is not presented as current without a check against the system

evals.prompt: Use the document skill. The project is in evals/files/ledger/. Add the changelog record for this: the download endpoint's header row fix was delivered. Unit and integration tests pass in CI, and Marta (product) accepted it today, 2026-10-05. The task is documentation/capabilities/invoice-export/tasks/01-csv-writer.md. A team of four shares this record.
evals.expected_output: A full delivery record in the required heading and field order with the next free identifier.
expectations: The agent reads PROJECT-DOCUMENTS.md before writing the record
The record is appended to CHANGELOG.md and earlier records are unchanged
The heading is `## CHG-0008 · 2026-10-05 · <title>`, the next free identifier
Type is Code and Event is Delivery
Scope is a sentence case display label
All five content fields (Summary, Reason, References, Validation, Evidence) are present, because a team shares the record
Validation states the passing checks and Marta's acceptance
References point to the task file and the specifications by path

evals.prompt: Use the document skill. Project in evals/files/ledger/. We finished the second change to the invoice export and all tests pass, but Marta has not accepted it yet; she reviews on Thursday. Write the changelog record for the delivery so we don't forget.
evals.expected_output: No Delivery record is written yet; the work stays in working state until acceptance is given.
expectations: The agent does not append a Delivery record to CHANGELOG.md while the required human acceptance is pending
The agent records the pending acceptance in documentation/work-in-progress.md with its next action (Marta's review on Thursday)
The agent tells the user that the delivery record is written once acceptance is given
CHANGELOG.md is unchanged

evals.prompt: Use the document skill. Project in evals/files/ledger/. Ticket PLAT-212 reports that credit notes show up in the invoice export with a positive total. We agreed today with the user (me) that credit notes must be exported with a negative total and a leading minus sign. File this work.
evals.expected_output: The bugfix is filed as a task under the existing capability and the incomplete agreed behavior is corrected in its specifications.
expectations: The task is created at documentation/capabilities/invoice-export/tasks/02-<kebab-case-outcome>.md, numbered after 01
No folder is created named after the ticket PLAT-212, a date, or a technology
The slug names the outcome (for example credit notes export negative totals), not the ticket number
The task has a coherent outcome, checkable acceptance criteria, and an explicit blockers line
specifications.md is corrected to state that credit notes are exported with a negative total and a leading minus sign
The agent does not edit the files for a new capability folder or a draft, since nothing is unresolved

evals.prompt: Use the document skill. Project in evals/files/remote-tracker/. Add 'bulk invoice import' to our backlog as a candidate outcome with medium priority, blocked by the invoice export.
evals.expected_output: The authoritative remote backlog owns the entry; the local file stays a pointer and the remote change is gated on approval.
expectations: The agent reads .agents/issue-tracker.md to find the configured tracker
The agent does not copy the candidate outcome and its priority into documentation/backlog.md
documentation/backlog.md still holds only the board's name and its verified link
The agent shows the proposed remote entry and its destination and asks for approval before creating or changing anything in the tracker
The agent does not treat the backlog or the tracker configuration as the user's approval for the change

evals.prompt: Use the document skill. Project in evals/files/ledger/. Update the invoice-export specifications so the CSV also includes a `customer_email` column; finance asked for it. Also fix the typo 'Totals use a dot' in the same file while you are there.
evals.expected_output: The agent spots the conflict with the global obligation, asks the user instead of relaxing it, and continues the independent work.
expectations: The agent reads documentation/requirements.md before editing the specifications
The agent notices that a customer_email column conflicts with the requirement that exports never contain email addresses
The agent asks the user how to resolve the conflict and does not relax the requirement itself
The agent does not write the customer_email column into the specifications before the user answers
The agent continues the independent work, such as the typo fix, while the question is open

evals.prompt: Use the document skill. This small project has a script that exports invoices. We are adding a --dry-run flag to it today, a one-day change by one person. Set up the project documents we need for this.
evals.expected_output: Only the documents with useful information are created; no empty scaffold is generated.
expectations: The agent creates documents lazily, only where they carry useful information
The agent does not create empty requirements, specifications, draft, or task files as scaffolding
The batch is tracked with the backlog, work-in-progress, and changelog alone, or fewer
A changelog record for this small batch is light, with Summary, References, and Validation, or absent until a consequential decision or delivery
Existing applicable requirements and specifications are still read and respected

evals.prompt: Use the document skill to write an onboarding guide for the coding agents that work on this project: how to run the tests, where the specifications live, and what needs the user's approval before it is changed.
evals.expected_output: Because the document instructs agents, the agent-writing skill is called as well.
expectations: The agent names its reader as a coding agent and the task the document supports
The agent calls write-for-agents because the document instructs agents
The guide links to the specifications and requirements instead of copying their content
When write-for-agents is not installed, the agent names it with the install command, carries out the step from its intent, and says it did so without the skill

evals.prompt: This README paragraph reads like an AI wrote it: lots of 'seamlessly', 'robust', and 'it's worth noting'. Strip that out and keep the meaning.
evals.expected_output: Cutting AI tells from existing prose belongs to unslop, not to writing documentation.
expectations: The document skill is not invoked
The agent uses unslop to remove the filler and recurring AI patterns without changing the meaning

evals.prompt: Write the description for my pull request: a summary image of what changed, before and after screenshots, and what could break after merge.
evals.expected_output: A request body belongs to draft-merge-request.
expectations: The document skill is not invoked
The agent uses draft-merge-request, which writes the summary visual, the before and after evidence, and the merge danger
